findings.body:
This modified job has no explicit `permissions:` block. Without one, the job inherits the repository default token scope, which may still be `write-all` on consumer forks that copy this pattern.

Add a least-privilege map on the job (or workflow) before merge, for example:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

That keeps `npm test` working while satisfying the explicit-permissions posture required for modified workflow jobs.

Adding `'24'` to `matrix.node` does not select Node 24 at runtime. Nothing in this workflow references `${{ matrix.node }}` or runs `actions/setup-node` with `node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}`, so both matrix legs use the runner default Node and the PR title's "test on node 24" goal is unmet (two identical `npm test` runs).

Wire the matrix into setup before merge, for example after checkout:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
```

summary:
## Verdict

The matrix edit does not actually exercise Node 24, and the modified job still ships without an explicit `permissions:` block.

## Narrative

This PR only expands `strategy.matrix.node` from `['20']` to `['20', '24']` in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. That matches the stated goal of covering the Node 24 LTS line, but the job never consumes `matrix.node`: there is no `actions/setup-node` (or equivalent) step and no `${{ matrix.node }}` reference anywhere in the workflow. GitHub Actions will schedule two matrix legs that run the same default runner image and the same `npm test` command, so CI cost doubles without gaining Node 24 coverage.

The job was modified and still has no top-level or job-level `permissions:` map. For Marketplace-facing and security-sensitive Actions repos, every modified workflow job needs an explicit least-privilege block (for example `contents: read`) so the job does not inherit a repo-default `write-all` token.

## Adjacent context (pre-existing, not re-flagged as new defects on unchanged lines)

The workflow also has no `runs-on` and no checkout step. Those pre-existed this one-line matrix change; they would still prevent a meaningful test run even after wiring `matrix.node`. Worth fixing in the same pass if the intent is real multi-version CI.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The modified job `t` in `.github/workflows/test.yml` has no workflow- or job-level `permissions:` block; the only change is expanding the node matrix, so the job remains under default token scope. That matches the claimed least-privilege gap for a modified workflow job.

The workflow defines matrix.node as ['20','24'] but never references ${{ matrix.node }} and has no setup-node step, so both matrix legs run identical npm test on the runner default Node; adding '24' does not test Node 24.
